title: Air India Deploys New Boeing 787-9 on Delhi–Toronto Route, Drops Vienna Fuel Stop
excerpt: The airline will eliminate its technical refuelling stop in Vienna from 1 August, cutting nearly three hours off the westbound journey and restoring daily service between India and Canada.
body:
• Air India will deploy its new Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on the Delhi–Toronto route from 1 August 2026, enabling non-stop westbound flights by removing the Vienna fuel stop.
  • Travel time on the Delhi-to-Toronto leg will drop from roughly 20 hours to about 17 hours, subject to airspace availability.
  • Daily service resumes after temporary frequency cuts in June and July 2026, rising from five weekly departures back to seven.
  • Premium Economy debuts on the route for the first time, alongside 30 Business Class private suites and an upgraded Economy cabin.

Air India will introduce its new Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on the Delhi–Toronto route from 1 August 2026, eliminating the technical fuel stop in Vienna that currently adds nearly three hours to the westbound journey. The change marks a significant upgrade for one of the airline's busiest long-haul corridors, cutting expected flight time from about 20 hours to approximately 17 hours.

The Toronto-to-Delhi return sector already operates non-stop, with a block time of up to 16 hours. That service will continue unchanged on the new aircraft.

Daily Flights Resume After Summer Cutbacks

Alongside the aircraft swap, Air India will restore daily Delhi–Toronto departures from 1 August. The airline had temporarily reduced frequency to five weekly flights during June and July 2026, citing unprecedented fuel price increases and broader geopolitical developments that disrupted global flight operations.

https://x.com/FinancialXpress/status/2079903245154091439

Under the new schedule, flight AI187 will depart Delhi at 01:45 and arrive at Toronto Pearson at 09:30 local time. The return AI188 leaves Toronto at 12:30, landing in Delhi at 14:05 the following day. All times are local.

Three-Class Cabin Brings Premium Economy to Canada

The line-fit Boeing 787-9 aircraft — with cabin interiors installed on Boeing's production line rather than retrofitted later — seat 296 passengers across three classes: 30 Business Class private suites, 28 Premium Economy seats and 238 Economy seats. The deployment marks the first time Air India has offered Premium Economy between India and Canada.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=AdomvUwSxiY

Business Class suites feature direct aisle access, 79-inch fully flat beds, wireless charging and a 17-inch 4K QLED HDR touchscreen. Premium Economy is configured in a 2-3-2 layout with 38-inch seat pitch, adjustable leg and calf rests, and a 13.3-inch screen. Economy passengers get ergonomically designed seats with 11.6-inch entertainment displays.

All cabins run the Thales AVANT Up entertainment system with more than 3,000 hours of content, Bluetooth audio connectivity, USB-A and USB-C ports, and AC power outlets.

"Canada is home to one of the world's largest and most vibrant Indian diaspora communities, and Toronto has long been one of Air India's most important international gateways. The introduction of our new Boeing 787-9 on the Delhi-Toronto route marks another important milestone."

— Campbell Wilson, CEO and Managing Director, Air India

Why the Vienna Stop Existed

The Delhi-to-Toronto sector requires a longer routing than the return leg because of regional airspace restrictions, according to Air India. The added distance previously forced the airline to make a technical refuelling stop in Vienna. The 787-9's superior fuel efficiency and range allow the carrier to cover the full distance without an intermediate stop — though the airline notes the non-stop operation remains subject to available airspace on any given day.

Air India previously operated the route with the larger Boeing 777-300ER, which lacked the range-per-seat economics to skip the stopover on the westbound leg. The transition to the 787-9 resolves that constraint while also upgrading the onboard product.

What It Means for the Indian Diaspora in Canada

Canada is home to more than 1.8 million people of Indian origin, and Toronto is the country's largest hub for the community. The upgrade directly benefits NRIs, international students, business travellers and families who regularly fly between the two countries. Dropping the Vienna stop removes the hassle of deplaning, clearing transit security and reboarding — a particular pain point for elderly passengers and families with young children.

The addition of Premium Economy also fills a gap that travellers had long requested: a middle-ground cabin between a ₹3–4 lakh Business ticket and a cramped long-haul Economy seat on a 17-hour flight.

Looking Ahead

The Delhi–Toronto deployment is part of Air India's broader fleet modernisation under the Tata Group's ownership. The airline has been progressively introducing new 787-9s and Airbus A350s on key international routes as it works toward its stated goal of becoming a world-class global carrier. Tickets on the upgraded Delhi–Toronto service are available through Air India's website, mobile app and travel agents worldwide.
nri_angle: Eliminates Vienna fuel stop and restores daily Delhi–Toronto service, directly benefiting the 1.8 million-strong Indian diaspora in Canada with faster, more convenient non-stop flights and a new Premium Economy cabin.
author: Diaspora Desk
